_doc: The chat input's editing surface. Its own pair rather than more keys in CLI_config because it is a different concern with a different reader: appearance is what the operator tunes, and these are BINDINGS — the thing somebody rebinds when their terminal sends something else. Every value here is data on purpose: a key map with literals in the code is a key map nobody can change without a diff.
_keys_doc: action -> the keys that perform it. A name beginning KEY_ is resolved against the curses module at load; anything else is the literal character get_wch returns, which is how control characters arrive (\u0001 is ^A). A name curses does not define is SKIPPED rather than raised — a terminal that lacks KEY_DC must not stop the client from starting.
_newline_doc: ^O, NOT Alt+Enter. In curses Ctrl-J IS \n and Enter arrives as \n, \r or KEY_ENTER depending on the terminal, so 'Enter sends, Alt+Enter breaks the line' cannot be told apart reliably — and a binding that works on the author's terminal and not the operator's is worse than an unfamiliar one. ^O is unambiguous everywhere.
_rows_doc: How tall the input strip may grow before it scrolls internally. The scrollback gives up a row for every row the input takes, so this is the trade between seeing what you are writing and seeing what was said.
_history_doc: How many sent messages Up/Down can walk back through. Recall fires only when the cursor is already on the first row, so it never fights with moving inside a multi-line request.
hint_line: ←→ move   ^A/^E ends   ^W word   ^O newline   ↑↓ recall   ⏎ send
